liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Mountains Of The Moon** (2 reviews): Reviewer finds this rendition very sweet, though an out-of-tune acoustic guitar slightly spoils it; Reviewer singles it out as a beautiful performance [3][13]
- **Doin' That Rag** (1 review): Reviewer's favorite of the show, partly because versions of this song are so rarely heard [14]
- **Dark Star** (1 review): Reviewer calls this version hypnotic and beautiful [13]
- **The Eleven** (1 review): A bad cut mars an otherwise nice version [12]

## Setlist highlights

- **Death Don't Have Mercy**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- **Mountains Of The Moon**: rare: 14 archived performances [15]

## The recordings

- **gd69-04-20.sbd.lutch.4992.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 10 songs; 105 min; rated 4/5 by 25 [1]. Said about its sound: The recording is hissy, muddy and quiet; The tape has some hiss and a slightly murky sound, but remains quite listenable; This transfer has much less hiss than the other version on archive.org, and is more complete [12][13][14]
- **gd1969-04-20.psbd.keshavan.1312.shnf**: source not stated; 4 songs; 36 min; rated 4/5 by 5 [2]

## Around the show

- Reviewer was a Clark freshman; this was their first Dead concert [5]
- Clark's student board booked many major acts despite a student body under 1500, including the Dead at least twice [5]
- Date is disputed: a poster says the 19th, while Deadbase says the 20th [6]
- At that earlier show the band played much Anthem material before the album was released [8]
- Reviewer recalls Paul MacGalliard running down the aisle toward the stage about forty minutes into that earlier set [8]
- Before Morning Dew, Jerry says on tape that the band's previous visit here was a disaster [9]
- Reviewer finds the 1969 sound distinctly different from the 1970s Dead, with spacey but melodic Dark Stars [9]
- Reviewer rates the Dark Star at least as good as the one played the following night [12]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd69-04-20.sbd.lutch.4992.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Rob Eaton and Jamie Lutch; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Two short dropouts in Morning Dew, at 3:29 and 7:19, were repaired with crossfades; A reel flip at the start of The Eleven was crossfaded; other flips fall between songs; No resampling or bulk waveform processing was done; fades begin and end the set [1]
- **gd1969-04-20.psbd.keshavan.1312.shnf**: transferred by Rango Keshavan; source: MSC>C>DAT>CDR>EAC>SHN [2]. Also: This pre-FM soundboard source, from Keshavan, holds all of the show that circulated as of August 1, 2000 [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1969-04-20 Grateful Dead Poster - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1969-04-20-grateful-dead-poster/) [16]
